answers.flag: B is also a documented design that meets the requirements (failover alias records over the weighted records, S3 website as secondary), so D wins only on the LEAST operational overhead tie-break (one added record versus renaming three records and adding two failover records); B also leaves out Evaluate Target Health = Yes, which the documented failover alias needs, so the stem leaves its correctness unclear.

A.quote: If a record in a group of records that have the same name and type doesn't have an associated health check, Route 53 always considers it healthy and always includes it among possible responses to a query.

B.quote: If you're using an Amazon S3 bucket for the secondary resource, specify the DNS name of the website endpoint.

C.quote: If none of the records in a group of records are healthy, Route 53 needs to return something in response to DNS queries, but it has no basis for choosing one record over another.

D.quote: If all the records that have a weight greater than 0 are unhealthy, then Route 53 considers the zero-weighted records.
